archetypes.name: Distrustful but content insider
archetypes.text: These respondents combine deep suspicion of other people and institutions with a surprisingly satisfied, even upbeat, view of democracy and their own finances. They report rising personal finances and feel their life is exciting, yet describe themselves as not too happy, a tension they rarely resolve. Their wariness extends to technology and AI, where they feel strongly uncomfortable and worried, while still backing more public science funding and rating their social lives as active. Trust in institutions is near zero, but faith in the system's functioning and personal progress stays intact.

archetypes.name: Distrustful but content insiders
archetypes.text: These respondents combine low interpersonal and institutional trust with a comfortable personal life. They feel little trust in people or institutions and are dissatisfied with how democracy works, yet they rate their finances as stable or improving and report being pretty happy. Many describe the economy as bad while still seeing their own situation as fine, and they are uneasy about AI and robots while often treating technology in mixed or contradictory ways. Routine socializing with friends or relatives runs alongside a wary, skeptical view of the wider world, which is the surprising pairing that defines the group.

archetypes.name: Distrustful financially strained skeptics
archetypes.text: People who distrust nearly every institution and other people, feel their finances are stuck, and see the economy as bad, yet still report being pretty happy. They tend to view life as routine while keeping close family ties, often seeing family time as more reliable than friendships. They consistently reject the idea that men's work harms family life or hold mixed views on it, express unease about AI and robots, and frequently call federal taxes too high. Their combination of deep institutional mistrust with personal contentment is the surprising core of this pattern.

archetypes.name: Distrustful but engaged skeptics
archetypes.text: People who are deeply dissatisfied with American democracy and the economy, yet remain politically engaged and actively verify political information online. Their financial outlook is bleak and family income feels far below average, but their general personal contentment is not uniformly low. A notable pairing is strong enthusiasm for automation and AI alongside a wish for more science spending and a fondness for routine, low-key social life. They tend to trust in institutions selectively, rather than uniformly high or low, and their views of taxes and social class are often inconsistent with their economic distress.

archetypes.name: Distrustful routine skeptics
archetypes.text: People who say you can't be too careful with others yet still check political information online, and who feel mostly unenthused about politics and democracy while staying pretty happy overall. They report a stalled, below-average family income and see themselves as lower class, but rate the economy as neither good nor bad and keep close ties with relatives. Their unusual mix is strong unease about robots and AI paired with ordinary, mid-level views on science spending and technology, so their worries about automation sit oddly beside their calm, routine outlook on life.

archetypes.name: Guarded middle-class skeptic
archetypes.text: Mildly trusting of people in general but cautious about institutions, while holding a comfortable middle-class financial outlook. Feels financially better off yet emotionally flat, with routine rather than exciting days and low happiness. Dissatisfied with democracy and uninterested in politics, yet actively verifies political information online. Ambivalent toward technology and AI, and relatively supportive of scientific funding. The mix of improving finances, low happiness, and disengagement is unusual.

archetypes.name: Distrustful, comfortable-with-tech skeptics
archetypes.text: These people are deeply distrustful of other people and of institutions alike, yet they are not disengaged: they find life exciting and feel their finances are improving. Their cynicism about politics and the economy coexists with optimism about personal circumstances. They are enthusiastic about technology and AI while being openly skeptical that science funding is worthwhile, a combination that runs against the usual pairing of institutional trust with pro-science views.

archetypes.name: Distrustful but content loners
archetypes.text: People who report low general trust and skepticism toward institutions and information online, yet feel financially secure and pleased with their own situation. They tend to be disengaged from politics and dissatisfied with democracy while not feeling unhappy in daily life, and they often show mild or strong discomfort with robots and AI taking over human tasks. Their social lives are thin and routine, with infrequent evenings out, and their views on family, technology and science are mixed, with some surprising mismatches between attitudes and everyday habits.

archetypes.name: Distrustful, disengaged, tech-skeptical
archetypes.text: Respondents here combine low trust in people and institutions with a strong habit of checking political information independently, which reads as wary rather than naive. They feel their families are financially worse off yet place themselves in the middle of the income range, and they describe economic conditions and democracy's performance negatively while staying politically uninterested. Their life outlook is flat, with dull routines but moderate social contact. Unusually, they strongly reject technology's benefits yet are not anxious about AI, and they want more public spending on science. Their attitudes cut across usual partisan or ideological lines, so they resist easy categorization.

archetypes.name: Distrustful, disengaged, economically strained
archetypes.text: Respondents combine deep distrust of institutions and of other people with low political engagement, yet they actively verify political information online, a pairing that looks contradictory. Financial dissatisfaction and a sense of worsening circumstances coexist with a self-placement in the working class and a view that taxes are too high. Social life is mixed: some describe life as dull or routine while still spending time with friends, and attitudes toward technology and AI are split, with many worried or uncomfortable yet not uniformly opposed.

archetypes.name: Distrustful but upbeat skeptics
archetypes.text: People who distrust others and institutions and feel little connection to politics, yet still describe their finances and personal lives as improving and their days as pretty happy. Their suspicion coexists with contentment, so they rate the economy poorly while personally feeling fine. They are often wary of AI and automation, sometimes deeply uncomfortable with machines doing human tasks, but may be enthusiastic about technology generally. Their social lives are thin, with infrequent friend contact and occasional family visits.

archetypes.name: Satisfied yet distrustful outsiders
archetypes.text: People who are highly content with US democracy and report being very happy, yet hold low trust in other people and in many institutions, and are wary of technology. Their satisfaction with their own finances and the economy sits alongside a sense of being financially behind average families and feeling their income is far below the norm. They lean toward tax resentment and see science as underfunded, while rarely socializing with friends outside their neighborhood or with relatives. The combination of political contentment, personal happiness, and social withdrawal with suspicion of others is unusual.

archetypes.name: Distrustful pessimistic institution-skeptics
archetypes.text: These respondents combine deep distrust of other people and institutions with bleak views of national democracy, the economy, and their own finances, yet they are not disengaged: many are highly interested in politics and actively verify information online. Their pessimism spans personal, social, and national levels at once, and they often feel worried about technology and automation while still describing ordinary family and social life as routine or moderately happy.

archetypes.name: Distrustful routine traditionalist
archetypes.text: Deeply distrustful of people and institutions, yet emotionally content and financially stable. Despite holding a very low opinion of democratic processes and public bodies, they report being very happy and feel reasonably well-off. Their life is routine and centered on family rather than outside social circles, and they hold traditional views on gender and work. They are skeptical of technology and automation, feel uneasy about robots and AI, and think science receives too much funding. The pairing of high personal contentment with thorough institutional cynicism is the distinctive feature.

archetypes.name: Distrustful disengaged skeptics
archetypes.text: People who distrust others and institutions yet describe their own lives as fairly stable and routine. Political disengagement and dissatisfaction with democracy often sit alongside a rating of their own finances as average or improving, a split between personal comfort and broader pessimism. Many are wary of AI and automation while still feeling their personal life is steady, and their social lives are sparse, with few evenings spent with friends or relatives.

archetypes.name: Trusting, upbeat, tech-wary traditionalists
archetypes.text: These respondents combine high generalized trust and strong satisfaction with democracy, finances, and life with a deep distrust of technology and AI, which is an unusual pairing for a group otherwise content with institutions. They feel financially improving yet see their income as below average, identify as middle class, and describe life as both exciting and very happy. Socially they keep a narrow circle, rarely spending evenings with outside friends but seeing relatives monthly. They avoid verifying political information online, dismiss work pressures on family life, yet want more public spending on science. Their optimism about personal life coexists with sharp anxiety about automation.

archetypes.name: Distrustful but socially engaged
archetypes.text: People who are deeply distrustful of others and institutions and dissatisfied with democracy and the economy, yet still report being pretty happy and find life exciting. Their political alienation and financial pessimism coexist with a warm, active family and social life, and they often rate themselves as working or middle class despite feeling their income lags behind average. Views on technology and AI are mixed, sometimes wary, and they are inclined to verify online political information while not necessarily following politics closely.

archetypes.name: Distrustful disengaged skeptics
archetypes.text: People who view others and institutions with deep suspicion yet remain politically passive and personally content. They distrust nearly every institution and feel democracy is failing, but rarely check political claims online and show little interest in politics. Their financial and social-class self-assessments are often moderate or positive, which sits oddly beside their dark views of the system. They feel uneasy about automation and AI, yet tend to be fairly ordinary in daily social life and routine. Their combination of wholesale mistrust with personal contentment and low civic engagement is the surprising feature.

archetypes.name: Distrustful low-trust skeptics
archetypes.text: People who see others as hard to trust and generally distrust institutions, yet are often politically engaged and check information online. Their wariness about people and institutions sits alongside a routine, stable private life and a fairly ordinary sense of financial security. They hold pessimistic views of the economy and democracy while still feeling personally content, and they tend to be cautious about technology and robots, but not overwhelmingly anxious about them.

archetypes.name: Distrustful satisfied routine skeptic
archetypes.text: People in this pattern distrust others and report being very satisfied with democracy while feeling uninterested in politics, a combination that suggests contentment with the system without engagement in it. Their personal finances feel improving yet they see their family income as below average and place themselves in the lower class, showing a gap between recent progress and perceived standing. They find life routine, happy but unexcited, and strongly favor traditional family roles, while sharply opposing technology and AI, which they regard with discomfort. They think science receives too much funding and taxes are too high, so their views on economics and innovation run against the usual pairing of optimism and trust.

Their pessimism about the economy and democracy sits alongside a routine, mostly content personal life and steady family ties. Their views on machines and AI are mixed, sometimes uneasy but rarely alarmed, and they often feel the country spends too much on research or taxes.

archetypes.name: Distrustful but content high-earners

Their low trust in others and in institutions sits alongside strong comfort with technology and a sense that life is exciting. They are wary of AI and robots while still feeling financially secure, and they tend to combine a self-reliant, skeptical stance toward public institutions with a personal life centered on family and social contact.

archetypes.name: Distrustful tech-comfortable skeptics
archetypes.text: People who distrust others and nearly all institutions, yet feel strongly comfortable with robots and AI and see science spending as excessive. Their outlook pairs deep wariness of people and public bodies with enthusiasm for technology. They are dissatisfied with democracy and the economy, but personally content, financially stable, and fond of family time. Surprisingly, they reject the idea that technology is a threat while doubting the value of publicly funded research.

archetypes.name: Distrustful but upbeat skeptics

They see themselves as middle class and personally comfortable, but rate the economy very good and their income far below average, a contradictory mix. They are enthusiastic about technology and not very worried about robots or AI, while wanting more public spending on science. The unusual pairing is generalized suspicion of others and institutions alongside personal optimism and contentment.
